# Temple Scroll Column 19 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** 11Q19 (Cave 11), Col. 19 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**19:1** And you shall take the one ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram.

**19:2** And you shall slaughter the ram and take its blood and dash it upon the altar round about.

**19:3** And the ram you shall cut into its pieces, and you shall wash its entrails and its legs,

**19:4** and put them upon its pieces and upon its head.

**19:5** And you shall make the whole ram smoke upon the altar; it is a burnt offering to the LORD, a soothing aroma, a fire offering to the LORD.

**19:6** And you shall take the second ram, the ram of the ordination,

**19:7** and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands upon the head of the ram.

**19:8** And you shall slaughter the ram and take from its blood and put it upon the lobe of the right ear of Aaron

**19:9** and upon the lobe of the right ear of his sons, and upon the thumb of their right hand, and upon the great toe of their right foot.

**19:10** And you shall dash the remaining blood upon the altar round about.

**19:11** And you shall take from the blood that is upon the altar and from the anointing oil, and you shall sprinkle it upon Aaron and upon his garments,

**19:12** and upon his sons and upon the garments of his sons with him; and he shall be holy, he and his garments, and his sons and the garments of his sons with him.

**19:13** And you shall take from the ram the fat and the fat tail and the fat that covers the entrails,

**19:14** and the appendage of the liver and the two kidneys and the fat that is upon them, and the right thigh — for it is a ram of ordination —

**19:15** and one loaf of bread and one cake of oiled bread and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread that is before Me.

---

*EMET notes: Column 19 is well preserved. It covers two sacrificial actions: the first ram (burnt offering, 19:1-5) and the second ram (ram of ordination/millu'im, 19:6-15), paralleling Exodus 29:15-23. The blood application to ear, thumb, and toe (19:8-9) is a distinctive ordination rite. The combination of altar blood and anointing oil (19:11) consecrates both persons and garments. "Fat tail" (alyah) refers to the broad fat tail of the Near Eastern sheep breed.*
